presets.title: L train: Canarsie Tube closed
presets.summary: 23,445 displaced riders an hour. If each takes the fastest open path, 4 segments overflow by 24,078 riders an hour: G Greenpoint Av → 21 St at 244%; G Nassau Av → Greenpoint Av at 201%; G 21 St → Court Sq-23 St at 198%; 4,689 have no open path. If riders are spread perfectly (max flow, forward peak direction), the open network can carry 17,167 of 18,432 (93%); 1,266 cannot move. Certificate: the flow is feasible, leaves no augmenting path, and its 17,167 equals the min cut's capacity, so FalkorDB's algo.maxFlow answer stands. The min cut holds no open segment: the open network has spare capacity everywhere these riders can reach, and only stations the closure cuts off limit the flow: origins 1 Av (1,266 riders an hour starting there); destinations 3 Av (315 riders an hour ending there).
presets.headroomSummary: 17,167 of 18,432 displaced riders an hour in the closure's forward direction can reach their destinations at all; the rest start or end at stations the closure cuts off (1 Av, 3 Av). Their demand can grow 1.77× before an open segment saturates; the first to fill: G Greenpoint Av → 21 St (spare 1,504 riders an hour) and G Metropolitan Av/Lorimer St → Broadway (spare 4,908 riders an hour). Found exactly in 4 certified max-flow solves on the fork.
